name: Kolar
headline: A KGF government school with four teachers for 86 students failed all 38 SSLC candidates in 2024.
summary: At a 126-year-old government school in Kolar Gold Fields, all 38 SSLC candidates failed in 2025 because four teachers served 86 high-school students with no Science or Hindi teachers. A report of a man marrying his bride's minor sister points to child-marriage pressure on adolescent girls. A claim about bus-fare barriers could not be tied to Kolar and was dropped.

reasons.detail: A KGF government school had four teachers for 86 high-school students and no Science or Hindi teachers; all 38 candidates failed SSLC in 2024.
A report of a man marrying his bride's minor sister shows child-marriage pressure on adolescent girls in the district.
Kolar stopped 93 child marriages in 2020-21, up from 17 in 2018-19 and 37 in 2019-20, a period linked in coverage to poverty and school closures during the pandemic.

reasons.factor: Gap between age cohort and secondary enrolment
reasons.detail: A district profile puts enrolment in classes 9-12 at about 60 percent of school-age children and says roughly 24 percent of girls aged 15-21 are out of education; years are not stated.
The education department ran a reopening drive to bring back 393 identified dropouts, with block and cluster resource persons tasked to track them; the report does not say why they left.
